notes: Summary: Verdigris builds an IDE platform with an always-on copilot; primary goal is seamless, low-friction completions with strict TTFT targets and deterministic token budgets.

Product ask: low-latency streaming + token budget tuning for IDE UX — TTFT for first token target <=70ms (warm), 150ms cold acceptable; end-to-end jitter <30ms p95; graceful backpressure when model slower.
Workload profile: high concurrency in editor (per-user incremental streaming), short completions (avg 32 tokens, max 256), heavy burstiness at commit / format events.
Model preferences: prefer smaller low-latency variants for primary completions; pinning per-editor version required so users get consistent behavior across releases.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper quantized model on Dedicated when latency SLOs can't be met; require traffic-splitting for canaries.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market — willing to pay for Dedicated capacity if it guarantees latency and predictable per-100k token pricing. Interested in Optimize recommendations to reduce spend.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML mandatory, need audit logs for code completions and retention controls (30/90/365 day tiers), KMS for inline encryption keys during POC.

POC timeline: - Week 0: onboarding + smoke tests (done 2025-11-20); - Week 2: baseline bench on hosted API (median TTFT 95ms, p95 210ms) (done 2025-12-02); - Week 5: token-budget tuning + continuous streaming integration (in progress); - Week 8: Dedicated sizing run + region failover test (planned).

Bench notes: baseline run (1k sessions) — warm first-token median 95ms, cold median 180ms; jitter spikes tied to KV cache misses and backend GC windows. Diego suggested KV prefetch + sticky routing for active sessions.

Engineering feedback: Verdigris CTO said on call: "We need deterministic behavior inside the editor — a jittery copilot is worse than a slower one." Wants explicit backpressure signals (429 vs partial stream) and client-side graceful degradations.
Integration asks: streaming SDK hooks for partial-token frames, client token budget API (can query remaining budget and request new budget per session), plugin-level model pin flag in config.json.
Security review: security team requested SOC2 attestation (in progress), sample audit log export for a week of completions, and KMS integration diagram. Drive link with security FAQ provided.
Commercial: procurement has asked for sample SOW for 12-month Dedicated commit + add-on for extended observability retention. Initial ARR estimate $120k-$150k depending on Dedicated sizing.
Current risks: failure to meet TTFT in APAC dev regions impacts product launch; procurement timeline slip if legal requires additional data residency clauses.
